review_note: Written from published youth training guidelines for a certified strength coach (CSCS) to review. Not coach-reviewed. Must never be shown to families as a real plan until review_status is 'approved'.

foundation.label: Foundation
foundation.who: All 8th graders, and any athlete with less than 1 year of supervised strength training.
rules: Technique first: an exercise only gets heavier when every rep looks the same.
No max-effort lifts and no 1-rep-max testing.

development.label: Development
development.who: 9th–12th graders with at least 1 year of supervised strength training and good technique on the main lifts.
rules: Heavier sets stop 2–3 reps short of failure.

block.progression: Weeks 1–2 learn the movements at the listed low end. Weeks 3–4 add a set or a little load if technique held. Week 5 is the hardest week. Week 6 drops volume by about a third so the athlete can retest.
block.retest: Retest the target stat at the end of week 6 and log it as a new entry.

season_phases.pre_season: Full plan, but strength work drops to the low end of the sets listed.
season_phases.in_season: Strength days drop to 1–2 per week at the low end of the sets listed. Speed and power work stays short and crisp. No added throwing volume for pitchers.
season_phases.rest_period: Baseball only. The yearly break from throwing (Pitch Smart). The throwing parts of every plan are removed; strength and movement work stays.

screens.question: Does the athlete have pain right now that changes how they move, throw or run?
screens.if_yes: No plan. Show: 'Get this checked by a doctor or athletic trainer before starting a training plan.'

screens.question: Baseball only: any pain in the throwing shoulder or elbow in the last month?
screens.if_yes: Remove all throwing work from the plan and show: 'Have the arm checked by a doctor or athletic trainer before adding throwing.'

screens.question: Has the athlete done at least a year of strength training with a coach watching their technique?
Where is the athlete in their season for this sport? (off-season, pre-season, in-season, or — baseball only — their yearly break from throwing)
How many team practices or games does the athlete have in a typical week?
screens.rule: Each practice or game counts as one hard day toward the tier's weekly limit. Strength days are dropped (C first, then B, then A) when the team schedule leaves no room for them.

exercises.name: Squat (goblet squat in Foundation, front or back squat in Development)
exercises.cue: Chest up, knees track over toes, full depth you can control.

exercises.name: Push-up (Foundation) / dumbbell bench press (Development)
exercises.cue: Body straight, elbows about 45° from the body.

exercises.name: Inverted row (Foundation) / dumbbell row (Development)
exercises.cue: Pull the elbow to the hip, pause at the top.

exercises.name: Split squat
exercises.cue: Front knee stays over the foot.

exercises.name: Nordic hamstring curl (partner-held, lower slowly)
exercises.cue: Lower as slowly as you can, catch yourself with your hands.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.cue: Straight line from head to feet.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift (dumbbells in Foundation, trap bar or barbell in Development)
exercises.cue: Push hips back, flat back, bar close to the legs.

exercises.name: Step-up
exercises.cue: Drive through the whole front foot; don't push off the back leg.

exercises.name: Pull-up or band-assisted pull-up
exercises.cue: Full hang to chin over bar.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.cue: Low back stays pressed to the floor.

exercises.name: Trap bar deadlift
exercises.cue: Stand tall fast; lower under control.

exercises.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
exercises.cue: Most of the weight on the front leg.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.cue: Don't let the band turn you.

focus_modules.name: Sprint speed
focus_modules.goal: Faster first steps and higher top speed.
focus_modules.added_to: The start of every strength day, right after the warm-up, while fresh.

work.name: Acceleration sprints from a 2-point or 3-point start
work.rest: Walk back plus about 1 min per 10 m

work.name: Flying sprints (build up 15–20 m, sprint 10–20 m)
Light sled or partner-resisted sprints (optional, only if equipment is available)

notes: Every rep is full effort with full rest. If times slow down, the session is over.
Run on a surface with good grip; no sprinting on wet grass in cleats that slip.

focus_modules.name: Jumping power
focus_modules.goal: More force in less time off the ground.
focus_modules.added_to: Strength A and Strength B, before the lifts.

work.name: Box jump (step down, don't jump down)
Broad jump, stick the landing
Pogo hops
Single-leg hop and stick
Medicine ball scoop toss for height (4–6 kg)

notes: Count foot contacts. Foundation stays around 40–60 per session; Development around 60–100.
Landings are quiet with knees over toes. Sloppy landings end the set.

focus_modules.name: Change of direction
focus_modules.added_to: Strength A and Strength B, after the warm-up.

work.name: Deceleration drill: sprint 10 m, stop in 3 steps, hold
5-10-5 shuttle at full speed
Lateral bound and stick

notes: Low hips on every cut; touch the line with the hand on the turning side.

focus_modules.name: Upper-body strength
focus_modules.added_to: Replaces the pressing exercise on strength days.

work.name: Barbell bench press (Development) / dumbbell bench press (Foundation)
Push-up with pause at the bottom
Extra row or pull-up set to match every pressing set

notes: Always use a spotter on barbell bench press.
Pull at least as much as you push, to keep the shoulders balanced.

focus_modules.name: Throwing velocity
focus_modules.goal: Throw harder by getting stronger and more powerful, without raising arm risk.
focus_modules.added_to: Medicine ball work on strength days; throwing on 3–4 separate days a week.

work.name: Rotational medicine ball throw into a wall (3–4 kg)
Step-behind medicine ball throw (2–3 kg)
Interval throwing program with a regular 5 oz baseball, distance building over the weeks
work.rest: At least 1 day between hard throwing days

work.name: Arm-care band work: external rotation, rows, Y-T-W raises

notes: No weighted-ball (overload) throwing in any plan.
After a throwing break, build back up over 4–6 weeks (ages 13–14) or 6–8 weeks (ages 15–18) before pitching off a mound.
Follow Pitch Smart pitch counts and rest days in games. Don't pitch on three days in a row.
Take at least 4 months a year off competitive pitching, with 2–3 months in a row of no overhead throwing.
Don't catch on days off from pitching.
Any arm pain: stop throwing and get it checked.

focus_modules.name: Catcher pop time
focus_modules.goal: Quicker transfer and footwork, and a stronger throw.
focus_modules.added_to: Throwing days, plus the throwing velocity strength and medicine ball work.

work.name: Transfer drill: receive and get to a throwing grip, no throw
Footwork-only reps to second base (no throw)
Full throws to second base

notes: Full throws count toward the day's throwing.
Pitchers who also catch: don't catch on rest days from pitching.

focus_modules.name: Rotational power
focus_modules.goal: Turn hip and trunk rotation into speed in the bat or the implement.
focus_modules.added_to: Strength A and Strength B, before the lifts.

work.name: Rotational medicine ball scoop toss into a wall (3–5 kg)
Medicine ball shot-put throw from the side stance
Landmine rotation
Sport skill at full intent (tee swings or standing throws)

notes: A lighter ball thrown fast beats a heavy ball thrown slowly.
Throws technique comes from the athlete's event coach; this plan builds the power behind it.

focus_modules.name: Speed endurance
focus_modules.added_to: One extra running day a week, plus the sprint speed module on strength days.

work.name: Repeat runs at about 85–90% effort
Hurdle mobility walkovers (hurdle events only)
Hurdle rhythm runs over low hurdles (hurdle events only)

notes: Never on the day after a hard strength day.
Hurdle technique comes from the athlete's event coach.

focus_modules.name: Distance running
focus_modules.goal: A bigger aerobic base and better pace control.
focus_modules.added_to: Running days on top of 2 strength days (Strength A and B only).

work.name: Easy runs at conversation pace
Steady tempo run
work.development: 1 × 15–20 min at a comfortably hard pace

work.name: Intervals at goal race pace
Strides

notes: Increase weekly running time slowly; a bigger week is followed by an easier one.
At least one full rest day a week.
Shin, foot or hip pain that gets worse while running: stop and get it checked.

not_trainable.message: Height isn't something a training plan can change. The plan focuses on the numbers the athlete can move.
Weight changes for teens should be planned with the athlete's doctor or a registered dietitian. The plan doesn't set weight or calorie targets.

plan_rules: Pick at most 2 focus modules: the trainable stats with the biggest gap to the next level, in the athlete's chosen sport(s).
Foundation: Strength A and B on non-consecutive days. Development: Strength A, B and C on non-consecutive days.
Focus work goes at the start of a session, after the warm-up, before the lifts.
Total hard days per week (strength, sprint, throwing at intent, interval runs) never exceed 4 in Foundation or 5 in Development, counting team practices the family enters.
Every plan shows the safety notes for its modules plus: 'Stop and tell a parent or coach about any pain. Pain is not part of training.'
Training replaces some practice time rather than piling on top of a full sport schedule.
